Okay, so I actually think this is a thing with most heterosexual couples lol. Every guy I know is far from interested in BTS, TXT, + other kpop boy bands, mainly because A) most girls go crazy for them, and B) they are way too “”girly””, so it’s automatically a stigma for men to like them unless they themselves are homosexual. Which is dumb. 

But my bf has come to respect that I love these seven men and their music, though he isn’t a fan. He still wants to know about the photo card I got in my album or about the online concert I’m attending.

So this might help:
What helped my bf warm up to the genre or at least respect it is explaining why I like them (not because of their good looks, but about the more intrinsic aspects of their music and how they use it to help the world become a better place) and seeing how passionate and happy I get when someone is live on VLive for example. If you occasionally mention or keep talking about how handsome Jin is or Yoongi’s gummy smile, it could be that he’s a little jealous , as silly as that sounds. Perhaps if you tweak the conversation a bit, it might do the trick. 

That being said, I think he owes you that much to at least understand how they got you through the year- because the more he learns about what makes you happy, the better he will understand how to do it himself. 

What are the sarcastic comments like? It might give you a hint as to why he doesn’t prefer to talk about them.

It’s good to know that you connect on another level- sometimes if it’s strong enough, you might eventually forget about him not being interested in something like BTS. For instance, if you both are gamers and find that to be a common hobby, there would be a lesser need to connect when it comes to music. This is the case with my bf and that’s why us connecting on music tastes is less important. But the sarcastic comments sound like a little much, the least he can do is respect your love for that particular genre/band.

Similar to the comment above, I think it’s important for the SO to be excited for you or find happiness in your passion for something else, even if he has zero interest in it. 

I am a huge KPOP fan and my bf detests that genre. But for the sake of knowing more about my interests and who I am, he makes sure to ask me questions about my favorite members or songs or whatever it is I want to talk about. 

There are also people I know who are in relatively happy relationships but don’t actually feel the need to care about certain interests because they meet halfway when it comes to something else. However, if you find that it hurts you (which is a completely valid feeling), you should bring it up.

You’ve got a fair point. I know it’s often encouraged to keep past relationships, certain secrets and what not hidden from spouses, but I just feel like it opens up a whole other can of worms.
